question: Where does the distance of our JOC objects to the objects of Dolby's decoder lie, and of what kind is it?
method: Every E-AC-3 track of a library of films that carries JOC, forty seconds of it from ten minutes in, cut out as it is (`ffmpeg -c copy`). Dolby's decoder wrote its objects (`dlbac3dec out-ch-config=21`, `docs/dolby-tools.md`): it is run as it stands and only what it writes is read. This decoder wrote its own (`decode --format damf --no-bed-conform`), with its dither and without it (`--no-dither`). `tools/joc_bands.py` compared the two object by object: the signal-to-noise ratio in 64 bands of 375 Hz, the same after the best linear fit, and the fit itself. An object under -70 dBFS is not counted: it is the noise of two decoders. A track is named by a number. The films are not in the repository.

a copy, the reference 100 samples late.expected: a lag of 100 and no difference at all

ours at half the level.expected: a ratio of 6.02 dB, nothing left after the fit, a gain of 6.02 dB and no phase

ours through a filter of three taps.expected: a low ratio, and a high one after the fit

ours with a noise of its own 30 dB down.expected: 30 dB before the fit and after it

ours with a noise below 300 Hz.expected: all of the difference in the lowest band, and no difference in the next

a channel of ours made mostly of another.expected: a large difference of the correlation of a pair, and none on a copy

a channel of ours a quarter turn behind.expected: no lag, a ratio of -3.01 dB, a high one after the fit in the lowest band as in all of it, and a fit of +90 degrees and no gain, which turns ours onto the reference

not_measured.why: Dolby's decoder wrote six channels and no objects
Dolby's decoder wrote six channels and no objects

the_lfe_beside_the_objects.how: the LFE of a track comes of the core decode and goes through no matrix and no filter of JOC; its ratio in the lowest band, on the tracks where it is over -70 dBFS, beside that of every object that is

below_750_hz.how: the ratio in steps of 11,7 Hz, the median over every object with signal in the lowest band, of every track

reading: Of 127 tracks with signal in the lowest band, 71 have that band more than 10 dB further from Dolby than the bands above it, and 36 more than 20: its ratio is 55.9 dB at the median where the bands from 375 Hz to 9 kHz have 71.4. The best filter on an object gains 1.9 dB of it at the median, so the two decoders do not differ by a filter on what they write. Inside the band the distance is largest at the bottom: 27.9 to 59.5 dB under 100 Hz, 68.1 to 100.0 between 400 and 750 Hz. The lowest subband is where this decoder takes the 90-degree phase shift of the downmix back out with a filter that was fitted to Dolby's decoder; what the fit left is this. The LFE, which goes through nothing of JOC, is at 115.9 dB in the same band on the 74 tracks that have one.
